title: Proposal detail page (list links to /dashboard/proposals/[id], which 404s today)
interface: Build the missing route app/dashboard/proposals/[id]. Follow the Clay layout contract in docs/design/clay-layout.md and copy the structure of the customer detail route (app/dashboard/customers/[id]/page.tsx, client.tsx, loading.tsx, not-found.tsx): server page.tsx fetches with getProposalById(id) from lib/actions/proposals.ts and calls notFound() when data is null; it also fetches the linked deal's name (deals.id, deals.name, scoped by organization_id via getOrgId like the actions do) when deal_id is set. loading.tsx uses PageSkeleton like the other loading files. client.tsx: usePageHeader({ backHref: '/dashboard/proposals', breadcrumbLabel: proposal.title, actions }) exactly as the customer detail does; actions = a 'Mark as sent' button only while status is 'draft' (calls markProposalSent, then router.refresh()). Body: PageHeader with the title and a status Badge (reuse the statusConfig labels/variants from app/dashboard/proposals/client.tsx: copy the map, do not import from that client file), then DetailLayout with main = the proposal content and aside = PanelSection 'Details' with a KeyValueList: Status, Deal (link to /dashboard/sales/<deal_id> when present, else an em dash), Valid until, Created, Sent, Viewed (dates via toLocaleDateString, em dash when null). Put all JSON parsing in lib/proposals/content.ts (pure, no React, no server imports), test-first in tests/proposal-content.test.ts: export type ProposalSection = { key: string; title: string; text?: string; items?: string[] }; export type PricingTier = { name: string; price: string; features: string[]; recommended: boolean }; export function parseProposalSections(content: unknown): ProposalSection[] and export function parsePricingTiers(pricingTiers: unknown, content?: unknown): PricingTier[]. parseProposalSections accepts a plain object; known keys render in this order with these titles: executive_summary 'Executive summary', problem_statement 'Problem', proposed_solution 'Proposed solution', solution_overview 'Solution overview', deliverables 'Deliverables', timeline 'Timeline', pricing_section 'Pricing', next_steps 'Next steps', terms 'Terms'; any other key whose value is a non-empty string or string[] follows, titled by turning snake_case into sentence case; string values become text, string arrays become items, anything else (objects, numbers, empty strings/arrays) is skipped; the key 'title' and 'pricing' are skipped; non-object input returns []. parsePricingTiers accepts (a) an object map of tiers like the seed's { good: {name, price:number, features}, better, best } in insertion order, (b) { tiers: [...] } from the AI pricing generator, (c) an array of tiers, and when pricingTiers yields nothing, falls back to content.pricing (the AI proposal's [{ tier, price, features }] array); name comes from name ?? tier; a numeric price is formatted as '$99/mo'-style '$' + toLocaleString('en-US') + '/mo', a string price is kept; features keeps only strings; recommended is true only when the tier has recommended === true; entries without a name are dropped. Render sections as Section blocks (h2-level title, text as whitespace-pre-line paragraph, items as a list) and pricing as a 'Pricing' Section containing a plain responsive grid of tiers (name, price, feature list, a 'Recommended' Badge when recommended); tier cards are the one legitimate box here, mark their wrapper data-clay-box. Empty content shows an EmptyState-style muted line 'This proposal has no content yet.'. Use existing components from components/dashboard/Page.tsx, components/ui and Icons; no new dependencies; do not modify the list page.

title: Seed stores the ids and shapes the UI filters on; migration 034 fixes rows already seeded
interface: The demo seed (lib/seed/generate.ts) writes display labels where the UI filters on ids, which empties tabs on Templates, Sequences, Playbook, Competitors and Contacts and breaks ICP detail. Test-first: extend tests/seed-generate.test.ts so every generated value is in the UI id set (hardcode the sets in the test), then change the seed. Mappings (label -> id): email_templates.category (UI ids general, cold_outreach, follow_up, nurture, re_engagement, meeting): Outreach->cold_outreach, Follow-up->follow_up, Proposal->general, Re-engagement->re_engagement, Scheduling->meeting, Onboarding->nurture. sequences.category (ids cold_outreach, warm_followup, re_engagement, post_demo, nurture): Nurture->nurture, Outreach->cold_outreach. objection_playbook.category (ids pricing, competition, timing, authority, need, implementation): price->pricing, trust->implementation; the others are already ids. competitors.category (ids direct, indirect, aspirational): 'Direct Competitor'->direct, 'Enterprise Competitor'->aspirational, 'Budget Competitor'->indirect. contacts.buying_role (ids economic_buyer, champion, technical_evaluator, end_user, blocker, coach): 'Decision Maker'->economic_buyer, Influencer->technical_evaluator, Champion->champion, Gatekeeper->blocker, 'End User'->end_user. icp_profiles.criteria must use the ICPCriteria shape in lib/actions/icp.ts (firmographic{industries, company_sizes, employee_range{min,max}, geography}, technographic{tech_stack, tech_sophistication_min}, behavioral{buying_patterns, trigger_events}, pain_points[{name, severity}], budget{revenue_range{min,max}, deal_size_sweet_spot, funding_stages}, channel{preferred_contact_methods, content_preferences}) and icp_profiles.weights the ICPWeights shape {industry, size, revenue, title, geography, tech} summing to 100. Convert the two seed profiles faithfully: industries <- industry, employee_range <- company_size.min/max, company_sizes <- every option of ['1-10','11-50','51-200','201-500','501-1000','1001-5000','5000+'] overlapping that range, geography, tech_stack, revenue_range.min <- revenue.min (max null), pain_points <- names with severities 8, 7, 6 in order, growth_rate '20%+ YoY' -> behavioral.trigger_events ['20%+ YoY growth']; weights: Enterprise SaaS {industry 20, size 25, revenue 20, title 10, geography 10, tech 15}, Growth-Stage Startup {industry 20, size 20, revenue 15, title 15, geography 15, tech 15}. Leave COPY_TEMPLATES categories alone. Then write supabase/migrations/034_normalize_seed_values.sql, a data-only migration in one transaction that rewrites rows already seeded with the old values, using exactly the same mappings: UPDATE ... SET category = CASE ... END WHERE category IN (<old labels>) for email_templates, sequences, objection_playbook, competitors, and buying_role for contacts; for icp_profiles, rebuild criteria with jsonb_build_object from the legacy keys only WHERE criteria ? 'industry' AND NOT criteria ? 'firmographic' (pain_points via jsonb_agg over jsonb_array_elements_text WITH ORDINALITY, severity = greatest(9 - ordinality, 1); company_sizes computed with the same overlap rule from company_size min/max; missing keys become the empty defaults) and replace weights WHERE weights ? 'company_size' with {industry, size, revenue, title, geography, tech} = {weights.industry, weights.company_size, weights.revenue, 10, weights.geography, 100 minus the other five} clamped to >= 0. Idempotent (re-running changes nothing). Header comment: what it fixes, that it is data-only, and that it must be run manually in the Supabase SQL editor. No schema, grant or RLS changes. Do not touch lib/seed/insert.ts or the UI.

title: Enrichment banner polls without overlap and backs off
interface: The banner is mounted on every dashboard page (app/dashboard/layout.tsx) plus some Lead Finder pages. The tracked-batch effect (components/lead-finder/EnrichmentProgressBanner.tsx, 'Poll the tracked batch's details') uses setInterval every POLL_INTERVAL_MS=2000 and never stops for a batch that is not progressing (the worker is not running), so with 3-19 s responses requests pile up (13 in flight observed) and slow every navigation. Fix: (1) new pure module lib/lead-finder/poll-delay.ts, test-first in tests/enrichment-poll-delay.test.ts: export const POLL_MIN_MS = 2000, POLL_MAX_MS = 60000; export function nextPollDelay(prevDelay: number, progressed: boolean): number returning POLL_MIN_MS when progressed, else min(prevDelay * 2, POLL_MAX_MS) (prevDelay below POLL_MIN_MS counts as POLL_MIN_MS). (2) Replace the setInterval in the tracked-batch effect with a setTimeout chain: load(), then schedule the next load only after the previous request settled (never two requests for the batch at once), delay = nextPollDelay(delay, progressed) where progressed means done/failed/status changed since the last response; stop when the batch is terminal (isTerminal) or the effect is cleaned up; while document.visibilityState is 'hidden' do not fetch (reschedule), and on becoming visible reset the delay to POLL_MIN_MS and poll once. Remove pollRef and POLL_INTERVAL_MS if no longer used. (3) Make the org-status refresh (refreshStatus / the active back-off effect) single-flight too: an in-flight ref so a call while one is pending returns without fetching; reuse nextPollDelay there in place of the inline doubling and drop STATUS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS / STATUS_POLL_MAX_INTERVAL_MS if unused. Keep every exported name, prop, the localStorage latch and the rendered UI unchanged.
